day.note: I'm Meowfia. I'll hold my Hawk claim and point out that Blair is the one who can't be a Hawk alongside me. That keeps the vote on Blair.

day.text: Drew, you say you visited me, but nobody visited my Kookaburra. My report isn't confused, so you're lying. Blair's Hawk claim stands. I'm voting Drew.
day.note: Drew says they visited me, but I was not visited: my dawn report wasn't confused and showed no change. So Drew's Hawk claim is false, which makes Drew the Meowfia.

day.text: Alex, you said you visited me as Eagle, but a Turkey gains an egg from every visitor and my nest is still 5. So that visit didn't happen. Your Eagle +1 is from Ellis. Drew and Blair both claim Hawk, but both of their visits check out. Alex's story is the one that's broken.
day.note: Alex's claim to have visited me is impossible: a Turkey gains an egg from each visitor, and my nest didn't change. Alex's Eagle +1 is explained by Ellis's visit, so Alex is lying about visiting me. Alex is my target.

day.text: Ellis says no one visited their Kookaburra, so Drew's visit to Ellis didn't happen. Drew, that makes your Hawk claim false. I'm throwing at Drew.
day.note: Ellis reports no one visited their Kookaburra, which contradicts Drew's claimed visit to Ellis. I'll side with the table on Drew, while avoiding any claim about my own role.

day.text: Finley, a Turkey doesn't gain from its own nest. It's the visitors who lay eggs in the Turkey's nest... so your nest staying flat proves nothing either way. My visit to you is real. Drew and Blair can't both be Hawk; I'm voting Drew, since Ellis and Blair both point there.
day.note: Finley misstates the Turkey: the Turkey gains nothing, the visitor lays the egg in the Turkey's... actually visitors get eggs, so my +1 is valid. Finley's claim that my visit didn't happen is wrong. Drew and Blair both claim Hawk; I'll go with Drew as the table leans.

day.text: Alex, a Turkey gains an egg from each visitor, so if you had visited me my nest would have grown. It didn't, so your visit didn't happen. Drew, Ellis says nobody visited their Kookaburra, so your Hawk claim is false. I'm throwing at Drew. Calling for the vote.
day.note: Ellis says nobody visited their Kookaburra, so Drew's Hawk visit is false, and Drew is the most likely cat. Alex's reply is also contradicted by the Turkey rule. I'll vote Drew and call for the vote.

day.text: Casey: Drew is my throw. CAW.
day.note: The table has settled on Drew, so I'll call CAW to end the day and throw one low card at Drew.

day.text: Ellis, if I visited you as Hawk you'd be confused, not reporting "nobody visited". Check your report again. I'm Hawk and I'm not throwing on a story that doesn't add up.
day.note: Votes are already forming on me. I'll say one line, and in eggsecution I'll throw a low card at Casey, the strongest accuser, to keep my high cards.

day.text: Drew is my throw. My Kookaburra wasn't visited, so Drew's Hawk claim is false. CAW.
day.note: Two CAWs are in. Drew's claimed visit to me didn't happen, so I'm pushing the vote on Drew to end the day.

day.text: Enough players have called CAW CAW: the day ends.

Alex.note: As Eagle I want to learn who visited a player. Pick Finley, who has been the most erratic in the last rounds and is a useful check.

Blair.note: I'm the Hawk and want to test whether Alex is Meowfia. Alex threw at me last round, and that's the most suspicious thing I've seen.

Casey.note: As Sphinx on Meowfia, I'll choose the Eagle role to learn who the Eagle is. The farm roles in play are Eagle, Hawk, Kookaburra, Turkey.

Drew.note: I'm the Floofer, Meowfia. Ellis is leading the scores and is likely a Farm information role, so hugging Ellis blocks their night action.

Ellis.note: I'm Farm, the Kookaburra. Visiting Alex, whose earlier story was shaky, to learn their role.

Alex.feeling: Messy and contradictory: two Hawk claims, a disputed Turkey gain, and a lot of confident accusations that don't quite add up.

Blair.feeling: Tense but manageable: Drew's false Hawk claim is exposed, though the table is muddled on Alex and Finley's stories.

Casey.feeling: As the Meowfia Sphinx, I know Alex is the Eagle, but the two Hawk claims and the conflicting visit stories make the day feel tangled and risky.

Drew.feeling: Tense. I'm the Meowfia Floofer, and the table has coalesced against my Hawk claim, with Casey, Finley and Ellis all throwing at me. Alex's and Finley's Eagle and Turkey stories don't reconcile, which gives me some room.

Ellis.feeling: Messy and contradictory: two Hawk claims, a broken Turkey and Eagle exchange, and Drew's visit claim looks false, so I'm fairly confident about Drew but unsure about the rest.

Finley.feeling: Messy and contradictory, with two Hawk claims and Alex's Eagle visit clashing with my Turkey nest, but Drew looks most likely to be the cat.

Alex.note: Table consensus is Drew, and Ellis's report contradicts Drew's Hawk visit. Throw my lowest card, C3.

Blair.note: Drew falsely claimed Hawk and the Kookaburra visit is contradicted, so Drew is the Meowfia target. I'm throwing a Wild and a 5 to add votes while keeping my high cards.

Casey.note: Throwing at Drew with one low card, H2, as a single vote.

Drew.note: Votes are heading to me. I'll throw my lowest card, H3, at Casey, the strongest accuser, so I lose as little as possible.

Ellis.note: Drew's visit claim contradicts my unconfused dawn report, so Drew is the Meowfia. Throwing my 9 at Drew banks it if Farm wins.

Finley.note: Drew is my throw, and the table is converging on them. I'll throw my two low cards, the 3 and the 7, and keep my 11 and 12s.

Alex.confusing: The Floofer and Kookaburra confusion rules were hard to track: I couldn't tell if a confused report meant my visit was wrong or just my dawn info. Confused players' reports made their claims unreliable for the whole table.
Alex.fun: Round 3, when Drew's Hawk claim fell apart because Ellis's Kookaburra report showed no visitor. Watching the table catch a lie through egg counts was satisfying.
Alex.change: Make the Eagle and Turkey egg rules clearer in the rules text, since several players, including me, misread who lays eggs in whose nest.
Alex.regret: In round 2 I threw at Blair, a Farm player, on Finley's Owl report, and I helped the Meowfia win. I would have questioned Ellis, who pushed hard for Drew and was actually Meowfia, and checked whose claims were consistent instead of following the loudest consensus.

Blair.confusing: The Kookaburra confusion rule was hard to track, since a confused dawn report can be wrong and I couldn't tell which claims to trust. It also wasn't clear whether a Turkey's nest should grow from visits in the way players were arguing.
Blair.fun: Round 3 was satisfying: the Hawk visit on Alex gave a clean result and exposed Drew's false Hawk claim, so the table converged on the real Meowfia.
Blair.change: I would make the dawn reports clearer about what a confused player can and cannot trust, so players aren't stuck guessing which claims hold.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I threw at Finley on a Floofer story I couldn't back, and my confused report left me unable to clear myself. Knowing Ellis was the Floofer, I would have pushed harder on Ellis's visit to me instead of splitting the throw.

Casey.confusing: The Eagle's gain rule was hard to track: Alex's +1 and Finley's Turkey story seemed to contradict each other, and the table never settled who actually visited whom. Also, the Falcon gains only when its target visited no one, which took the table too long to work out.
Casey.fun: Round 2's day, where Blair refused to name a visitor and the table slowly caught the broken Falcon story, was the most engaging stretch. The vote pile-on on Blair felt tense.
Casey.change: I would make the dawn reports clearer about visitors, since many claims were built on unverifiable or confused reports. Clearer reports would make the deduction less about guessing who was lying.
Casey.regret: In Round 3, as Meowfia, I pushed the vote onto Drew, my own teammate, and called CAW to end the day, which cost my side the round. I should have stayed quiet or thrown at a Farm player like Alex, since the table was split and I could have kept Drew alive.

Drew.confusing: The Turkey and Falcon egg rules caused real confusion: several players, including me at first, misread when Falcon gains and who lays eggs in a Turkey's nest, and it took days to settle. Alex's false Kookaburra and Turkey claims also made the visit-and-egg math hard to check.
Drew.fun: Round 2, when the table argued over the Falcon rule and then corrected itself, showed how a claim can be checked against the egg counts. Winning the Falcon argument while Blair couldn't explain their +2 was satisfying.
Drew.change: Make the rules and dawn reports clearer for Turkey, Falcon, and Eagle, and state plainly which players were confused. Also show each player's visit count in the day summary so claims are easier to test.
Drew.regret: I used my Wink on Ellis in round 1, but Ellis was an honest Farm Owl whose report was accurate. I should have kept the Wink and pointed the table at Alex, whose Kookaburra story was the actual weak point.

Ellis.confusing: The Falcon's gain rule was easy to misread: it lays an egg only when its target visited no one, and I initially called Drew's claim impossible. The Floofer's hug effect was also unclear to me as a Meowfia player.
Ellis.fun: Round 3 was satisfying: my Kookaburra showed an unvisited nest, which exposed Drew's false Hawk claim and got the table to vote them out.
Ellis.change: I would make the dawn reports clearer about which eggs come from which visitor, since several players' stories hinged on it.
Ellis.regret: In round 2 I wrongly called Drew's Falcon story broken and piled onto a true Farm claim. I should have checked the Falcon rule before pushing suspicion.

Finley.confusing: The Owl's visitor report was the most confusing part. It listed only animals, not players, so I couldn't tell who the Floofer was, and that led me to the wrong target.
Finley.fun: Round 1 went well: the Ellis collapse and the Drew vote came together, and Farm won with a 6-vote throw.
Finley.change: I would make dawn reports name the players who visited, not just the animals. That would make the night deductions much clearer.
Finley.regret: In round 2 I dropped my Drew suspicion after misreading the Falcon rule and threw at Blair, a Farm player, losing my 11 and Wild. I would have kept pressing Drew, or looked harder at Ellis, who was the Floofer and the real Meowfia visitor.

review.title: The Lone Cat Wins
review.headline: Ellis won round one dead, round two as a cat, and the game.
review.summary: In round 1 the Mouser Drew winked the Owl Ellis, which exposed him, and Farm threw him out. In round 2 Ellis was the lone Meowfia. He hid behind a misread Falcon rule while Farm threw out the Farm Kookaburra Blair. In round 3 Drew's false Hawk claim was broken by Ellis's clean report, and Farm won again. Ellis finished first with 28 against Blair's 15, helped by a banked 8 in round 1 and a solo cat win worth 5 in round 2.

rounds.recap: Drew, the Mouser, named himself and then winked the Owl Ellis, which gave Farm an obvious target. Alex's confused report made him look shaky too, but the Wink tipped everyone onto Drew. Farm won, and the dead Ellis still banked an 8.

Only Ellis was Meowfia. Finley's Owl report of a Floofer on Blair was true, but Blair's confused report left him unable to answer. The table first wrongly attacked Drew over the Falcon rule, then switched to Blair. Blair was eggsecuted and Ellis won alone.

Drew, a Floofer, claimed Hawk against the real Hawk Blair. Ellis's unconfused Kookaburra report said nobody visited him, which disproved Drew's claimed visit. Everyone threw at Drew, so Farm won and the Sphinx Casey lost.

highlights.text: Drew winked Ellis mid-day, and the death itself pointed the table at the only Mouser claim.
Drew's Falcon claim was torn down by the whole table, then Drew re-read the rule and everyone, Ellis included, reversed.
A true Owl report, one Floofer visited Blair, got a Farm player eggsecuted because Blair's confused report left him no defence.
Ellis's clean Kookaburra report contradicted Drew's claimed Hawk visit and sealed the vote.

confusions.what: Claimed a Kookaburra visit and Floofer result and puzzled over Casey's Falcon claim without recognising his own confused report.
First said a Turkey gains only from visitors and that Drew's claim failed, then reversed. He later misread the Falcon rule.
As the Falcon he said Alex's Turkey egg explained his gain, and his claim only held up after a long debate.
Said a Falcon that visited someone cannot gain an egg, misreading the 'target visited no one' condition.
Said Drew's Falcon story was impossible, then reversed after Drew's re-read.
Said a Falcon that visited Alex gains nothing, a misreading of the rule.
Accused Drew over a Falcon misreading and later apologised.
Argued that his Turkey nest staying at 5 proved Alex did not visit him, but a Turkey lays eggs in visitors' nests, not its own. Alex's +1 was an Eagle gain from Ellis's visit.
Claimed his Eagle +1 came from visiting Finley, but an Eagle gains per visitor to its target, and he was the only visitor.
Said Alex's +1 came from the Turkey egg, mixing up Turkey and Eagle.

worked: Confused Kookaburra reports in rounds 1 and 2 were a real puzzle, because players had to decide how far to trust unreliable data.
Cross-checking dawn reports decided round 3: Ellis's unconfused report disproved Drew's claimed visit.
Hawk and Mouser visit info combined with the Owl's report to expose Drew in round 1.
The Wink death in round 1 was a vivid moment, though it backfired on the winker.
problems: The scoring snowballs. A round-1 banked 8 plus a solo cat win left Ellis far ahead, and nobody changed their play against the leader. Fix: reduce rewards for dead players or tie-break against the leader.
Players barely acted on the standings. Despite the rules' stress on outscoring teammates, throws followed the consensus every round, and the leader was never targeted.

Round 2 turned on a Farm player being eggsecuted for being confused. Confusion plus a Floofer hug left the Kookaburra with no usable defence, so the lone cat won almost for free. Consider a confusion signal that is useful to the confused player.

The Falcon and Turkey/Eagle texts are easy to misread. Many players got them wrong across rounds 2 and 3, which wasted discussion time. Fix: use plainer wording such as 'gain an egg if your target visited nobody'.
Votes converged on one target almost at once in every round, so the vote was rarely in doubt. Wild and low-card throws cost nothing, which also removes risk. Fix: make small throws cost something.
